parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation and documented social acceptance/tourism welcome, with a 2024 entry programme easing passport-mismatch scrutiny, support a relatively safe visitor experience. That is offset by weakly enforced anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime law or bias-data, a 2025 killing prosecuted as ordinary crime, a documented hospital-ward refusal, and dated but severe custody exposure to men's prison/solitary for non-medically transitioned trans women. Custody and ward placement are the worst documented exposures; current rules and programme coverage at all ports are unresolved, so protections cannot be credited as fully operative.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign passport may not match appearance/gender; resident documents cannot change marker, but visitor document is home-issued.
entry_documents.protection: National immigration pride-welcome programme launched 5 August 2024 eases scrutiny for mismatched passports.
entry_documents.interaction: Programme may smooth arrival, but operation at every port and written procedure are not sourced; later document checks remain uncertain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Dated cases show men's-prison placement against request, harassment and forced exposure in 2015; elsewhere men's cells or solitary absent medical verification.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: LGBT prisoners separated nationwide since 1993; one coastal remand prison held trans inmates in dedicated block in 2016-17; capital LGBT-prison pilot announced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a visitor were detained, current placement rule, pilot status and foreign-visitor routing are unresolved, so dated protections may not operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Hospital refused post-operative trans woman a women's ward; no bathroom/facility law for visitors is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented facility-access ban; dedicated prison block is a limited facility protection in one institution.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Ward placement in emergency/inpatient care could out visitor and cause misplacement, with no documented remedy.

care_services.exposure: Care settings not uniformly respectful; ward refusal documented, without date or remedy.
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming surgeries since 1975, puberty blockers and hormones available; free hormone treatments reported in 2025 reporting.
care_services.interaction: Medication continuity is comparatively accessible for residents/visitors, but ward placement and record respect remain inconsistent.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence documented; 2015 equality act weakly/spotty enforced, only 44% LGBTQ awareness in 2019 survey.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Equality act bans gender-identity discrimination with penalties up to 6 months and fine; marriage equality since January 2025 signals institutional acceptance.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Paper protection is weakly enforced and does not document operative relief for a short-stay visitor; resident gaps are climate only.

minors_guardians.interaction: No visitor-facing rule on travelling minors, guardianship, school or care for minors is documented; resident adoption/surrogacy rules are not credited or deducted.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: April 2025 foreign tourist murdered trans woman in coastal city after refusal for sex; community called it hate crime. 2019 resident survey: 8% police harassment, 11% physical abuse.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Social climate reported as accepting, with greater acceptance and little opposition to trans laws; tourism-hub positioning.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Single 2025 killing should not dominate rate assessment, but no hate-crime enhancement or bias-data collection shows thin recourse; 2019 figures are resident/local-sphere and dated.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No hate-crime designation as of November 2025; no bias-motivated crime data; equality-act implementation spotty/inadequate in 2021 report.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equality act and courts exist in principle, but no documented visitor remedy succeeding is provided.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainties include pride-programme port coverage, current prison placement, hospital-ward remedy, and outcome/charges in 2025 killing.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar ward-by-record placement and uneven care denial, but this dossier has wider hormone/surgery access, a dedicated entry programme and stronger documented social acceptance, placing it above 0.55.

0.65-A has brief detention followed by apology, compensation and reliable court-ordered release. Here custody risk is more severe on dated evidence and remedies are weakly enforced, so it sits below 0.65.
0.65-B's care refusal was overturned within hours by an ombudsperson. Here ward refusal has no documented reversal and hate-crime recourse is absent, making operative protection weaker.

0.75-C accepts matching markers, provides tribunal appeal and brief detention ending in release. Here entry easing is recent but coverage is unsourced and custody placement may be by birth/medical status, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: social acceptance and entry welcome reduce everyday street/border risk, and no trans-specific crime is documented. The operative risk concentrates if outed in institutional settings—hospital ward or detention—where dated birth/medical-status placement, solitary/men's cells and weak anti-discrimination enforcement leave little proven remedy. Those state-imposed exposures, unresolved current practice, and absent hate-crime recourse pull the case from Reduced toward the top of Elevated, despite welcoming climate.
